newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-Swedbank to buy stake in HSB bank.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Swedbank to buy stake in HSB bank.

text.p: One of Sweden's big four banks, Swedbank, on Tuesday grabbed a slice of newcomer HSB Bank in the continued restructuring of the Swedish banking sector.
Swedbank said it intended to pay 52 million crowns for a 9.1 percent stake in HSB Bank, a banking unit of co-operative real estate company HSB Sverige AB that will start in October.

Swedbank said it would buy the stake by subscribing for shares in a new share issue. It has a conditional call option for a further 3.4 percent stake in HSB Bank which will be a bank for co-operative flats.
"Swedbank and HSB have had a close cooperation for many years," said Swedbank, adding that it was a natural development to take a stake in HSB Bank
The two banks will cooperate on clearing, technical operations, fund operations and first mortgages.

"It's not such a big deal but it shows that players are talking to each other," Fredrik Myren, analyst at HSBC James Capel, told Reuters. "The groups have been cooperating and they have the same philosophy - they both have a very popular profile."
The deal is the latest reshuffle in the Swedish banking sector as banks prepare to meet fearsome intrnational competition ahead of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) from January 1, 1999.
In addition, mergers and cooperation can trim information technology costs as the banks have to update computer systems anyway ahead of both EMU and the turn of the century.

In June Swedbank announced it was about to acquire 7.4 percent of shares in Estonian bank Hoiupank. Swedbank is also in the process of merging with Swedish rival Foreningsbanken to ForeningsSparbanken.
Two local savings banks, Sparbanken Finn and Sparbanken Gripen, that previously cooperated with Swedbank, preferred to stay out of the merger and instead bought a stake in JP Bank.
Early this year Handelsbanken bought mortgage lender Stadshypotek for 22.9 billion crowns.
The changes and accompanying market rumours have fuelled bank shares.
A much speculated merger between S-E-Banken and state-controlled Nordbanken failed in the spring.
Market players continued to speculate about a marriage between the two banks but last week a new rumour of a merger between S-E-Banken and Handelsbanken took the spotlight.

The banks never comment on rumours but analyst expect another large deal to emerge this year, probably involving Nordbanken as the government's 1997 budget includes sales revenues from its 59.4 percent stake in the bank.

The government has calculated on getting 16 billion crowns for its shares but as the share price has rocketed it could pocket as much as 30 billion, analysts say, adding that the government would love to have that money to woe voters ahead of a September 1998 general election.
HSB Bank will become a subsidiary of HSB Sverige. It will have a restricted equity of more than 450 million crowns and a balance sheet total of about nine billion crowns.

The HSB group has 570,000 members and in the year 2000 it expects to have 50 percent of the total co-operative flat production and a total market share of at least 10 percent of all new Swedish housing.
